Definition: a tiara, i.e. official turban (of a king or high priest)
BiblicalUsage: The word is the mitre, the turban of the high priest, and it belongs to the holy garments: the plate of pure gold was fastened upon the mitre, and the mitre was put upon Aaron's head at the consecration.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the mitre is the crown of the priest: holiness to the LORD was written on the gold, and the priest wore it on his forehead where all could see.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
